visualLearning.intro: Five complementary views compress the already-published PA-S001 theory for review. They distinguish P0's publication mechanics from learner evidence; they do not assess mastery or claim production operation.

modes.label: Mind map
modes.title: P0 connects three different objects
modes.rationale: The session is foundational and structural: a compact map makes the relationships among theory, implementation, evidence, scope, quality, and boundaries visible before examining individual modules.

diagram.title: PA-S001 engineering foundations mental map
diagram.description: A mental map of PA-S001 connecting theory, implementation, evidence, architecture, quality, boundaries, coupling, frontend platform architecture, AI product engineering, and Staff-to-Principal scope.

cards.title: The public chapter
cards.body: site/ holds the canonical public learning material. A chapter can exist before its lab runs; that is publication, not proof of learning.

cards.title: The renderer
cards.body: site/tooling reads explicit bilingual content, validates its bounded contract, and writes static routes. It represents the material rather than becoming the material itself.

cards.title: What still needs observation
cards.body: A successful scaffold check does not demonstrate learner understanding, semantic translation quality, accessibility, or production operation.

modes.label: Boundary flow
modes.title: What reaches the public output
modes.rationale: Publication and trust boundaries are central to the session, so the existing Mermaid topology is the most direct way to show distinct public products and excluded inputs.

diagram.title: P0 public publication boundary
diagram.description: The separate portfolio route and bilingual Learning Site routes are generated from explicit sources; data and artifacts are not copied automatically.

cards.title: Portfolio ≠ Learning Site
cards.body: The portfolio is a professional surface. The Learning Site is the canonical home for the complete session theory.

cards.title: Explicit inputs are not a security control
cards.body: The allowlist limits automatic copying, but public content still requires review; a folder alone does not enforce access or truthfulness.

modes.label: Scope matrix
modes.title: Application, system, and platform answer different questions
modes.rationale: PA-S001 explicitly distinguishes levels of scope. A side-by-side representation prevents treating a shared folder or two consumers as automatic evidence of a platform.

rows: Application
A user-facing purpose such as the Book
What outcome does this product provide?
It can hide the build and delivery dependencies needed to publish it.
System
Chosen elements and relationships: content, build, and delivery
Which dependencies and failure paths matter here?
Its boundary must be chosen; it is not automatically the whole ecosystem.
Platform
Capabilities, contracts, and support for consumers
Can more than one meaningful consumer adopt this safely?
A shared package or one use case does not alone establish a platform experience.

modes.label: Change journey
modes.title: A content change crosses a bounded publication path
modes.rationale: The theory explains how a named editorial change propagates and where a missing reference stops it. A sequence makes the normal and failure paths easier to reason about than a prose-only description.

diagram.title: Session publication change flow
diagram.description: A content change is catalogued, validated, and generated; a missing translation or R999 causes an identifiable build error before the output is replaced.

steps.title: Edit an explicit source
steps.body: An editor changes a bilingual session page under site/.

steps.title: Load the expected pair
steps.body: The build reads the known ES and EN paths rather than copying arbitrary repository data.

steps.title: Validate the editorial contract
steps.body: Shape, cited identifiers, and structural correspondence are checked; semantic equivalence still needs human review.

steps.title: Generate public routes
steps.body: Only after validation does the renderer write dist/ for the static host.

steps.title: Stop a malformed publication
steps.body: A missing R999 or translation produces an identifiable failure rather than a silently published Mermaid or malformed page.

modes.label: Flashcards
modes.title: Test distinctions, not vocabulary alone
modes.rationale: Several PA-S001 terms are easy to collapse into each other. These prompts ask for the boundary or consequence that distinguishes them, without reporting a score or mastery level.

cards.question: What distinguishes engineering and architecture, and what change would test it?
cards.answer: Software engineering is the discipline of specifying, building, verifying, operating, and maintaining software. Architecture concerns an entity’s fundamental concepts and properties in its environment; an architecture description is the artifact expressing them. This distinction keeps ordinary code edits and diagrams from being mislabeled as architecture [R1] [R2].
cards.explanation: Model: intended outcome → responsibilities → contracts → change → verification. Constructed example: publishing a bilingual chapter requires content, validator, generator, and routes; changing a button color affects presentation, while moving content validation changes responsibilities and failure modes. Counterexample: a correct diagram does not prove that the produced site respects its boundaries. Documenting decisions costs time and is useful when a change affects consumers or qualities; in production, compare the description with tests and output rather than treating intent as behavior.

cards.question: What distinguishes application, system, platform, and ecosystem, and what change would test it?
cards.answer: An application serves a user goal. A system is the elements and relationships within a chosen boundary. A platform offers capabilities to consumers through interfaces, support, and adoption rules; an ecosystem includes surrounding participants and providers [R5] [R13].
cards.explanation: Model: the Learning Site is an application; content, compiler, host, and browser form the publication system under analysis. A shared theme package may be a system component, but it is not automatically a platform: consumer compatibility, adoption, and operations contracts are still needed [R13]. Counterexample: calling two pages with shared CSS a platform overstates the capability. Widening the boundary reveals host or supplier failures but increases analysis cost; in production, choose scope according to the decision and dependencies that can fail.

cards.question: What distinguishes quality attributes and constraints, and what change would test it?
cards.answer: A quality attribute is an evaluable product property, such as accessibility, maintainability, or security; a constraint limits allowed solutions. ISO/IEC 25010:2023 offers a product quality model, not a measurement of this site [R3].
cards.explanation: A verifiable scenario identifies source, stimulus, environment, artifact, response, and measure. Proposed example: when a section translation is missing during build, validation fails before replacing output and names the section. “Must be accessible” does not specify a testable response [R4] [R15]. Strict validation costs schema maintenance as content changes; its expected benefit is detecting structural drift. A schema test does not certify semantic translation or Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 conformance; manual review remains necessary [R15].

cards.question: What distinguishes boundaries and contracts, and what change would test it?
cards.answer: A boundary assigns responsibility to an element and determines what information crosses to another. A contract defines observable inputs, outputs, errors, and compatibility; a directory alone enforces none of these. Parnas proposes decomposing modules around decisions likely to change [R12].
cards.explanation: Constructed example: `site/` stores public content; validation accepts pages with valid sections and citations; generation publishes declared routes only. A missing reference stops the build. That publication boundary does not establish that every public sentence is true. Counterexample: recursively copying the repository into `dist/` could cross the publication boundary and include private data. An explicit allowlist costs maintenance; production review must inspect both the list and the included text.

cards.question: What distinguishes coupling and cohesion, and what change would test it?
cards.answer: Coupling is dependence between elements: changing one can require changes elsewhere. Cohesion asks whether responsibilities inside a module serve a related purpose. Separating likely change decisions, as Parnas recommends, lets both properties be examined through concrete elements [R12].
cards.explanation: Constructed example: the generator depends on the `Page` contract, not on every Spanish sentence. Changing section IDs also affects links, cards, and map: coupling exists even without imports between files. A cohesive validator concentrates editorial invariants. Counterexample: moving every function into `shared/` does not prove cohesion and may add cross-dependencies. Lower coupling costs interfaces and coordination; in production, observe change propagation, failures, and compatibility before claiming improvement.

cards.question: What distinguishes frontend platform architecture, and what change would test it?
cards.answer: Frontend Platform Architecture (FPA) designs reusable frontend capabilities and their consumer experience: interfaces, documentation, compatibility, support, and adoption. It relates to platform engineering; the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) model considers investment, adoption, interfaces, operations, and measurement [R13].
cards.explanation: Constructed example: a theme capability consumed by site and portfolio would need tokens, a change contract, and tests for both consumers. Sharing CSS or one function today does not prove that such a platform exists. Reading layout and progress rules remain product responsibilities. Counterexample: extracting a generic design from one use case fixes assumptions too early. A platform costs maintenance and support; in production, justify it through actual consumers and repeated changes, not folder preference.

cards.question: What distinguishes ai product engineering, and what change would test it?
cards.answer: AI Product Engineering (AIPE) integrates artificial intelligence (AI) as a product capability with evaluation, operations, and risk management. Using AI to write code does not by itself add an AI product feature. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) addresses AI-system risk [R6].
cards.explanation: Hypothetical example: a session recommender retrieves evidence, generates a proposal, checks citations, and abstains when data is missing. A well-formed response does not prove accuracy. Sculley and coauthors describe technical debt caused by dependencies and coupling in machine-learning systems [R14]. Counterexample: assigning L1–L5 from a recommendation without evidence turns a suggestion into certification. Evaluation, observability, and human review cost effort; production requires failure and escalation criteria before relying on the capability. P0 does not integrate a model.

cards.question: What distinguishes staff and principal scope, and what change would test it?
cards.answer: Staff and Principal name responsibility scopes that vary by organization, not universal skill levels. GitLab provides a contextual example that distinguishes group technical leadership from a wider Principal framework [R7] [R9]. A documented decision does not prove actual influence.
cards.explanation: Hypothetical example: Staff agrees on the Book evidence contract with one team; Principal proposes compatibility and exception policy across systems and teams. The mechanism is a wider coordination radius and ownership of cross-system consequences, while decision owners remain clear. Counterexample: enforcing one pattern without adoption-cost evidence can transfer work to other teams. Coordinating more systems costs time and requires observed outcomes; production consequences cannot be inferred from a title or an Architecture Decision Record (ADR).

cards.question: How does the model connect outcome, responsibility, change, and verification?
cards.answer: Concept and scope: the central model of this session connects outcome → responsibility → change → verification. The outcome is observable behavior; responsibility assigns who produces it; change exposes dependencies; verification compares actual behavior with the contract. This is a teaching synthesis grounded in engineering and architecture description, not a new standard [R1] [R2].
cards.explanation: Mechanism: in P0, a reader requests a route; the generator has transformed validated content into HTML; the browser shows theory and stores local study marks. The publication contract limits what enters `dist/`; canonical progress and mastery levels remain outside. Review compares routes, citations, controls, and empty states with output.

sections.title: Objective
paragraphs: Connect purpose, structure, quality, and evidence to initialize P0. This chapter is an initial editorial synthesis of PA-S001; it neither establishes mastery nor replaces the full Theory Phase in the conversation.
Phase: F0 — Accelerator Platform. Simultaneous areas: Frontend Platform Architecture, AI Product Engineering, and Staff engineering, with an introduction to Principal-level scope.

sections.title: Learning Preview
paragraphs: Scope includes engineering and architecture; application, system, platform, and ecosystem; quality and constraints; boundaries; coupling and cohesion; FPA; AIPE; and Staff/Principal scope. These concepts apply to the Book without forcing an AI feature into it.

sections.title: Concepts
paragraphs: Software engineering covers development, operation, and maintenance through a systematic, disciplined approach [R1]. Architecture supports reasoning about system structure, behavior, and qualities [R2]. In this program, a responsibility defines what an element owns; a contract states what consumers can expect. These are tools for analyzing changes, not promises of superiority.

ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 distinguishes an architecture from an architecture description: the latter expresses the former rather than replacing it [R11]. A route map or an ADR is therefore evidence of a description, not proof that the described structure has the intended quality.

sections.title: Main Topic — A justifiable system
paragraphs: Concept and scope: the central model of this session connects outcome → responsibility → change → verification. The outcome is observable behavior; responsibility assigns who produces it; change exposes dependencies; verification compares actual behavior with the contract. This is a teaching synthesis grounded in engineering and architecture description, not a new standard [R1] [R2].

Mechanism: in P0, a reader requests a route; the generator has transformed validated content into HTML; the browser shows theory and stores local study marks. The publication contract limits what enters `dist/`; canonical progress and mastery levels remain outside. Review compares routes, citations, controls, and empty states with output.

Synthesis: P0 connects theory, implementation, and evidence, but these objects do not mean the same thing. A chapter may exist before its lab runs. A test may pass without demonstrating learner understanding. Presentation must preserve these differences. site/ holds canonical public material; site/tooling renders it. artifacts/ and data/ are not automatically copied to the output. This is an Accelerator rule that must be checked against generated output. Its cost is maintaining an explicit editorial contract; its expected benefit is limiting incompatible interpretations. The hypothesis alone does not demonstrate greater maintainability.

A change travels through named elements: an editor changes site/en/sessions/PA-S001/page.json; ContentValidator checks shape and cited identifiers; SiteGenerator writes dist/; SessionPage presents the data; SessionTOC links to section anchors. A TypeScript type can state the expected data shape, but it cannot by itself prove that a translation file exists or that the two texts express the same meaning. The build checks file loading and structural correspondence; bilingual editorial review remains a human verification.

Counterexample: a folder list that calls shared code a “platform”, or a green test used to declare mastery, breaks the verification chain. The model requires naming the changed outcome, its owner, the contract protecting consumers, and the observation that confirms behavior. It costs editorial coordination and correspondence checks; its limits include semantic translation and human assessment. In production, those gaps need review before publication or decision acceptance [R2] [R12].

sections.title: Subtopics S1–S8
paragraphs: Each subtopic develops one concept in the P0 context: definition and scope, mechanism, constructed example, counterexample, cost, limit, and production consequence.

sections.title: S1 — Engineering and architecture
paragraphs: Concept and scope: Software engineering is the discipline of specifying, building, verifying, operating, and maintaining software. Architecture concerns an entity’s fundamental concepts and properties in its environment; an architecture description is the artifact expressing them. This distinction keeps ordinary code edits and diagrams from being mislabeled as architecture [R1] [R2].

Mechanism: Model: intended outcome → responsibilities → contracts → change → verification. Constructed example: publishing a bilingual chapter requires content, validator, generator, and routes; changing a button color affects presentation, while moving content validation changes responsibilities and failure modes.

Architecture focuses on decisions about overall structure and behavior [R2]. Hypothetical example: fixing a link is localized; defining session identity across languages constrains multiple consumers. Significance does not depend on line count. As a heuristic, examine scope, change cost, and affected qualities. Choosing technology first may hide alternatives; documenting every minor decision also has a cost. The learner must explain why a Book decision deserves architectural treatment.

Mechanism: a structural decision becomes consequential when it narrows or enables later changes. Moving the renderer from a static generator to a server, for example, changes delivery, operational responsibility, and failure modes. A component’s folder location does not. The contrast prevents treating ordinary implementation edits as architecture while still making actual architectural constraints explicit.

Counterexample: a correct diagram does not prove that the produced site respects its boundaries. Documenting decisions costs time and is useful when a change affects consumers or qualities; in production, compare the description with tests and output rather than treating intent as behavior.

sections.title: S2 — Application, system, platform, and ecosystem
paragraphs: Concept and scope: An application serves a user goal. A system is the elements and relationships within a chosen boundary. A platform offers capabilities to consumers through interfaces, support, and adoption rules; an ecosystem includes surrounding participants and providers [R5] [R13].

Mechanism: Model: the Learning Site is an application; content, compiler, host, and browser form the publication system under analysis. A shared theme package may be a system component, but it is not automatically a platform: consumer compatibility, adoption, and operations contracts are still needed [R13].

Operational definitions: an application serves a user purpose; a system includes elements and relationships within a chosen scope; an ecosystem includes participants and providers. A platform provides capabilities around consumer needs [R5]. The Book is an application. For publication analysis, its system includes content, building, and delivery. A shared package does not establish a platform experience: contracts and support also matter. Scope avoids both ignoring dependencies and unnecessarily modeling the entire environment.

For example, PortfolioPage and SessionPage may consume a future shared theme capability, but that does not make the current two-page use case a frontend platform. Compatibility policy, versioning, documentation, support, and at least more than one meaningful consumer are separate concerns. Extracting too soon creates a generic API whose assumptions may not fit either product.

Counterexample: calling two pages with shared CSS a platform overstates the capability. Widening the boundary reveals host or supplier failures but increases analysis cost; in production, choose scope according to the decision and dependencies that can fail.

sections.title: S3 — Quality attributes and constraints
paragraphs: Concept and scope: A quality attribute is an evaluable product property, such as accessibility, maintainability, or security; a constraint limits allowed solutions. ISO/IEC 25010:2023 offers a product quality model, not a measurement of this site [R3].

Mechanism: A verifiable scenario identifies source, stimulus, environment, artifact, response, and measure. Proposed example: when a section translation is missing during build, validation fails before replacing output and names the section. “Must be accessible” does not specify a testable response [R4] [R15].

Quality scenarios specify source, stimulus, environment, artifact, response, and measure [R4]. Proposed example: an author adds a missing reference during a build; the validator rejects publication and identifies that reference. This is a criterion, not a measurement. Static output is a program constraint; a particular tool is an option. Immediate publication and bilingual human review may conflict: resolving that tension requires a process decision, not just code.

The normal path is therefore not only rendering: it is validate both language inputs, then replace generated output. The failure path stops before a malformed reference enters the output. This gives a bounded integrity property, but it does not measure latency, prove source truthfulness, or certify accessibility.

Strict validation costs schema maintenance as content changes; its expected benefit is detecting structural drift. A schema test does not certify semantic translation or Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 conformance; manual review remains necessary [R15].

sections.title: S4 — Boundaries and contracts
paragraphs: Concept and scope: A boundary assigns responsibility to an element and determines what information crosses to another. A contract defines observable inputs, outputs, errors, and compatibility; a directory alone enforces none of these. Parnas proposes decomposing modules around decisions likely to change [R12].

Mechanism: Constructed example: `site/` stores public content; validation accepts pages with valid sections and citations; generation publishes declared routes only. A missing reference stops the build. That publication boundary does not establish that every public sentence is true.

Software design separates responsibilities, architecture, components, and interfaces to satisfy functional and quality requirements [R1]. Hypothetical application: a reader interprets storage while a view consumes interpreted content. Changing format should preserve the contract if the separation hypothesis holds. A folder does not prevent access or provide a security control. Check who reads each input and what is published. In P0, an explicit public-file list avoids indiscriminate data copying; it does not replace review of content written inside those files.

P0 has product boundaries (portfolio versus learning site), module boundaries (content validation versus rendering), execution boundaries (local preview versus static host), publication boundaries (explicit inputs to dist/), and trust boundaries (reviewed public text versus private artifacts). Treating all five as folders would hide different failure mechanisms.

Counterexample: recursively copying the repository into `dist/` could cross the publication boundary and include private data. An explicit allowlist costs maintenance; production review must inspect both the list and the included text.

sections.title: S5 — Coupling and cohesion
paragraphs: Concept and scope: Coupling is dependence between elements: changing one can require changes elsewhere. Cohesion asks whether responsibilities inside a module serve a related purpose. Separating likely change decisions, as Parnas recommends, lets both properties be examined through concrete elements [R12].

Mechanism: Constructed example: the generator depends on the `Page` contract, not on every Spanish sentence. Changing section IDs also affects links, cards, and map: coupling exists even without imports between files. A cohesive validator concentrates editorial invariants.

Coupling describes interdependence; cohesion describes internal relationships among tasks or elements [R10]. Example: duplicating ES/EN references requires coordinated changes even without imports between files. Shared identifiers may reduce divergence, but a shared error may affect both languages. Less duplication does not automatically mean less coupling. Grouping everything in shared does not prove cohesion either. The learner should study a concrete change, observe propagation, and explain why responsibilities belong together or apart.

ContentValidator is cohesive when it owns parsing and input invariants, while SessionPage is cohesive when it owns presentation. Giving SessionPage direct filesystem reads would couple HTML layout to storage. A typed contract reduces accidental shape mismatch, but it does not remove coupling to route names, reference conventions, or the build order. Those dependencies require deliberate tests and documentation.

Counterexample: moving every function into `shared/` does not prove cohesion and may add cross-dependencies. Lower coupling costs interfaces and coordination; in production, observe change propagation, failures, and compatibility before claiming improvement.

sections.title: S6 — Frontend platform architecture
paragraphs: Concept and scope: Frontend Platform Architecture (FPA) designs reusable frontend capabilities and their consumer experience: interfaces, documentation, compatibility, support, and adoption. It relates to platform engineering; the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) model considers investment, adoption, interfaces, operations, and measurement [R13].

Mechanism: Constructed example: a theme capability consumed by site and portfolio would need tokens, a change contract, and tests for both consumers. Sharing CSS or one function today does not prove that such a platform exists. Reading layout and progress rules remain product responsibilities.

Curricular definition: FPA designs shared frontend capabilities, contracts, and adoption experience. It applies the consumer-oriented platform principle to frontend work [R5]. A reusable theme needs an understandable interface and compatibility; a rule approving a session belongs to the product, not necessarily a generic component. Generalizing from one case can embed premature assumptions. PA-S001 starts a real consumer and leaves future extractions as open decisions. No time savings are claimed without measuring adoption and maintenance.

In this slice, the semantic shell, responsive CSS, language links, and disclosure TOC are shared delivery mechanisms, not a declared design system. The portfolio has its own navigation and deliberately does not render the chapter. Future extraction must be justified by compatible consumers and an adoption contract, not by a preference for a shared folder.

Counterexample: extracting a generic design from one use case fixes assumptions too early. A platform costs maintenance and support; in production, justify it through actual consumers and repeated changes, not folder preference.

sections.title: S7 — AI product engineering
paragraphs: Concept and scope: AI Product Engineering (AIPE) integrates artificial intelligence (AI) as a product capability with evaluation, operations, and risk management. Using AI to write code does not by itself add an AI product feature. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) addresses AI-system risk [R6].

Mechanism: Hypothetical example: a session recommender retrieves evidence, generates a proposal, checks citations, and abstains when data is missing. A well-formed response does not prove accuracy. Sculley and coauthors describe technical debt caused by dependencies and coupling in machine-learning systems [R14].

Curricular definition: AIPE integrates, evaluates, and operates Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a product capability. Using Codex to write code does not add AI to the product. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AI Risk Management Framework addresses AI-system risks and characteristics [R6]. Hypothetical example: an assistant recommends sessions, but a recommendation is not mastery evidence. Useful results, abstention, and failures must be distinguished. Evaluation needs cases and criteria tied to purpose. Review costs effort and does not eliminate all errors. This scaffold neither calls models nor introduces credentials.

A valid JSON response from a model is only a format result. Factual correctness requires a separate grounded claim, source review, and evaluation set. A safe product can abstain when evidence is unavailable and can expose uncertainty rather than manufacture a level or metric. P0 models that boundary by rendering no AI feature and keeping mastery null until evidence exists.

Counterexample: assigning L1–L5 from a recommendation without evidence turns a suggestion into certification. Evaluation, observability, and human review cost effort; production requires failure and escalation criteria before relying on the capability. P0 does not integrate a model.

sections.title: S8 — Staff and Principal scope
paragraphs: Concept and scope: Staff and Principal name responsibility scopes that vary by organization, not universal skill levels. GitLab provides a contextual example that distinguishes group technical leadership from a wider Principal framework [R7] [R9]. A documented decision does not prove actual influence.

Mechanism: Hypothetical example: Staff agrees on the Book evidence contract with one team; Principal proposes compatibility and exception policy across systems and teams. The mechanism is a wider coordination radius and ownership of cross-system consequences, while decision owners remain clear.

GitLab provides one specific example: Staff generally operates within team domains and Principal at organizational scope [R8] [R9]. This is not a universal title mapping. Program synthesis: progress from coordinating system decisions to technical direction across systems. Staff example: agree on the Book evidence contract. Principal example: propose compatibility, ownership, and exceptions for multiple consumers. Enforced uniformity may transfer costs to other teams; total divergence also has costs. A lab ADR does not demonstrate real organizational leadership.

The programme labels L1 Explain, L2 Implement, L3 Operate, L4 Decide, and L5 Lead are its own evidence vocabulary, not an industry standard or percentage scale. They help separate receiving an explanation from operating a system or leading a decision. No level is assigned in this chapter; proof must be attached to actual work.

Counterexample: enforcing one pattern without adoption-cost evidence can transfer work to other teams. Coordinating more systems costs time and requires observed outcomes; production consequences cannot be inferred from a title or an Architecture Decision Record (ADR).

sections.title: Theory → Practice Map
paragraphs: Canonical content → site/. Presentation → site/tooling/render.ts. Editorial contract → content.ts. Publication → build.ts. Learner evidence → data/mastery/PA-S001.json, initially empty. Scaffold tests check bounded cases of structure, references, and HTML output; they establish neither comprehensive accessibility nor mastery.

sections.title: Time Breakdown
paragraphs: The following are study estimates, not observed learner times: 45–60 minutes for concepts and main topic; 60–90 minutes for the developed subtopics; 30–45 minutes for the examples and source review; and 30–60 minutes for exercises and evidence preparation. Actual duration, if later recorded, must not overwrite these estimates without a source.

sections.title: Real-World Example
paragraphs: GitLab provides its own contextual career ladder: its Staff material addresses technical leadership within a group, while its Principal framework describes scope equivalent to a stage [R7] [R9]. This is not a universal title definition. The contrast is useful for reasoning about radius of influence, coordination, and cross-system consequences; it cannot establish the learner's capability, level, or outcomes.

External fact: the GOV.UK Design System publishes components with usage guidance and code examples [R16]. Inference for P0: documenting component contracts could help future adoption; this case does not prove P0 works or is accessible.

sections.title: Production-Ready Example — constructed example
paragraphs: Constructed example, not an existing system: an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted tax-document review system receives a request, retrieves documents, calls an AI adapter, and validates that every suggestion cites retrieved evidence. The normal path sends a recommendation with evidence identifiers to a human reviewer; it also records telemetry and the applied policy version. The design treats traceability and human review as product controls aligned with AI risk management [R6].

Failure path: if retrieval fails, citations are absent, or validation rejects the result, the service degrades to insufficient-evidence and does not present a recommendation as supported. The human reviewer retains the decision and can request more documents. This degradation does not prove the policy is correct: it is proposed behavior that avoids turning a well-formed response into an unsupported tax conclusion.

Proposed future tests: simulate retrieval_failed, missing_citations, and validation_failed; assert that each evidenceId belongs to the retrieved set; verify that telemetry carries policy version without recording sensitive documents; and review the human flow for accessibility. Limitations: the contract does not evaluate legal correctness, retrieval coverage, bias, credential security, or cost. None of these tests exists in P0 yet.

sections.title: Curated Sources and References
paragraphs: The cited references support distinct technical claims: SWEBOK for engineering [R1], ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 for architecture description [R2], ISO/IEC 25010 for quality [R3], NASA for scenarios [R4], Baldwin and Woodard and CNCF for platforms [R5] [R13], Parnas for modularity [R12], NIST and Sculley et al. for AI risk and technical debt [R6] [R14], GitLab as a contextual scope example [R7] [R9], W3C for accessibility [R15], and GOV.UK for component guidance [R16]. P0 examples remain constructed or local; those sources do not prove P0 outcomes.

paragraphs: For study, reread the cited source sections and turn one quality attribute into a scenario with source, stimulus, environment, artifact, response, and measure. A later Architecture Decision Record (ADR) must record learner reasoning rather than copy this editorial synthesis.

sections.title: End-of-Session Success Criteria
paragraphs: First runnable app; reviewed ES/EN pages; documented actual tests; controlled failure diagnosed by the learner; reasoned ADR; recorded evidence and limitations. A functioning scaffold neither completes the session nor replaces the full theory chapter.
checklist: The portfolio and Learning Site are separate public routes with no fabricated professional information.
ES and EN pages, indexes, breadcrumbs, language links, theme control, and static generation have been mechanically checked.
The learner has supplied actual evidence before any mastery or Completed status is recorded.
Manual accessibility and responsive reviews are recorded as performed rather than inferred from a build.

sections.title: Bridge to PA-S002
paragraphs: PA-S002 evolves the same repository through monorepo and engineering standards: workspace/app/package, dependencies, public APIs, and quality gates. Pending work becomes Revisit and never blocks another session.

sections.title: Evidence and current status
paragraphs: Current state: there is no learner-supplied implementation or learning evidence, and no L1–L5 level is assessed. Checklist and exercises are learner-controlled study state; session status may be Not started, Partial, Completed, or Revisit, whereas L1–L5 requires real evidence. Artifacts, tests, and measurements count only when they exist and are recorded. This page is editorial synthesis; its constructed examples are not P0 results.
